subject: social_science
chapter_title: Outcomes of Democracy: Accountability, Growth and Dignity

concepts.title: Accountable, Responsive and Legitimate Government
concepts.definition: A democratic government is judged on whether it is accountable to citizens, responsive to their needs and legitimate in the eyes of the people, since it follows procedures and consults before decisions rather than acting overnight like a dictatorship.
concepts.key_idea: Democracy may be slower in reaching decisions, but it builds support through deliberation, and its legitimacy rests on the people's free choice of rulers.
question_patterns: how is a democratic government accountable to its citizens
why is democracy called a legitimate government
compare democratic and non democratic governments on responsiveness
why do democratic decisions take longer than dictatorial ones
how does democracy ensure transparency in decision making
what makes a government legitimate in the eyes of the people

solution_steps.explain: Check whether citizens can question decisions, obtain information about them, and change rulers through elections.
Look at whether government attends to citizens' needs and follows established procedures of consultation.
A democratic government is people's own government, so even its critics accept it as legitimate, unlike rule by force.

concepts.title: Economic Growth under Democracy and Dictatorship
concepts.definition: When growth rates of regimes are compared over 1950-2000, dictatorial regimes averaged 4.42 per cent against 3.95 for democracies, so the difference is the dictatorship rate minus the democracy rate.
concepts.key_idea: The gap of about half a percentage point is small and cannot prove that dictatorships deliver better development, since inequality and war also shape outcomes.
question_patterns: calculate the difference in growth rates between democratic and dictatorial regimes
how much faster did dictatorships grow than democracies between 1950 and 2000
compare the economic growth of democracies and dictatorships
find the growth gap when both regime rates are given
does dictatorship deliver higher growth than democracy explain
what do the growth tables of 1950 to 2000 show

solution_steps.explain: Take the average growth rate of dictatorial regimes and subtract that of democratic regimes to get the gap

concepts.title: Gap between Top and Bottom Income Shares
concepts.definition: Inequality within a country can be read from the difference between the national income share of the top 20 per cent and that of the bottom 20 per cent of the people.
concepts.key_idea: In Brazil the top fifth holds 63 per cent of income against 2.6 for the bottom fifth, while Denmark's 34.5 against 9.6 shows democracies vary widely in income fairness.
question_patterns: calculate the gap between the income shares of the richest and poorest twenty per cent
find the inequality gap for a country from its income share table
how much larger is the top income share than the bottom share
compare income inequality in brazil and denmark
compute the difference between top 20 and bottom 20 per cent shares
what does the inequality table tell about economic disparities

solution_steps.explain: Take the income share of the top 20 per cent and subtract the share of the bottom 20 per cent

concepts.title: Accommodation of Social Diversity
concepts.definition: Democracy handles social differences best when every community gets a chance to be heard and rule by majority means rule by any group that wins support, never rule by a single community in its own interest.
concepts.key_idea: Democracy stays viable in deep diversity as long as no one community tries to dominate others and citizens weigh reasons rather than identities.
question_patterns: how does democracy accommodate social diversity
what does rule by majority actually mean in democracy
why is democracy suitable for deeply diverse societies
when does democracy fail to accommodate diversity
distinguish between majority rule and rule by majority community
how should majorities treat minorities in a democracy

solution_steps.explain: Majority rule means any group that forms a majority through elections, not a permanent ethnic or religious majority.
Check whether all communities have a voice, and whether decisions consider minority views.
Democracy fails when a majority community denies others a share in power, turning politics into domination.

concepts.title: Dignity and Freedom of Citizens
concepts.section: Dignity and freedom of the citizens
concepts.definition: Democracy's strongest claim is its promise of dignity and freedom: it rests on the principle of political equality, expanding recognition for all individuals including lower castes and women, even when practice falls short of expectation.
concepts.key_idea: Democratic struggles have spread respect for individual freedom and dignity, and democracy's merit is that conflicts over dignity can be openly fought and corrected.
question_patterns: how does democracy promote the dignity of citizens
explain how democracy expands the idea of freedom
how has democracy helped women and lower castes claim equality
compare expectation and achievement of dignity in india
why is political equality central to democracy's outcomes
what does democracy offer that dictatorships cannot on dignity

solution_steps.explain: The principle of political equality recognises the worth of every individual, supporting claims of dalits and women.
Check for freedoms of expression, association and movement that let citizens argue for their rights.
Note that societies take time to live up to ideals, but democratic politics lets excluded groups press their claims.

concepts.title: Assessing the Outcomes of Democracy
concepts.section: How do we assess democracy's outcomes
concepts.definition: Judging democracy means asking what we expect of it: accountable and legitimate rule, economic well being, reduced inequality, accommodation of diversity, and dignity for all, tested against its record rather than against perfection.
concepts.key_idea: Democracy's success is not measured only by economic performance but also by its ability to correct itself and keep improving, which is a constant process without a perfect endpoint.
question_patterns: how do we assess the outcomes of democracy
what should we expect from a democratic government
is democracy better than dictatorship in reducing inequality
explain the ongoing process of improving democracy
why is democracy judged by more than economic growth
list the criteria to evaluate democracy's performance

solution_steps.explain: Frame the test: accountable government, economic development, equality, diversity handling and dignity.
Use growth and inequality data to test each expectation instead of accepting or rejecting democracy blindly.
Democracy's advantage is the continuous chance to complain, discuss and improve outcomes through citizens' participation.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Between 1950 and 2000, all dictatorial regimes grew at {dictatorial_rate} per cent a year while all democratic regimes grew at {democratic_rate} per cent. Calculate the growth gap in percentage points.

solution_template.explain: Take the average growth rate of dictatorial regimes and subtract that of democratic regimes to get the gap

worked_examples.question_pattern: Poor countries under dictatorship recorded {dictatorial_rate} per cent growth against {democratic_rate} per cent for poor democracies. Find the difference in their growth rates.

solution_template.explain: Take the average growth rate of dictatorial regimes and subtract that of democratic regimes to get the gap

worked_examples.question_pattern: In Brazil the top 20 per cent of people hold {top20_share} per cent of national income and the bottom 20 per cent hold {bottom20_share} per cent. Calculate the inequality gap in percentage points.

solution_template.explain: Take the income share of the top 20 per cent and subtract the share of the bottom 20 per cent

worked_examples.question_pattern: A country's income table shows the richest fifth with {top20_share} per cent of national income and the poorest fifth with {bottom20_share} per cent. Find the gap between the two shares.

solution_template.explain: Take the income share of the top 20 per cent and subtract the share of the bottom 20 per cent
